title: HB524 (2019 Regular): Firearms; prohibit public employers from banning employees with permit and training endorsement from carrying on property.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2019/html/HB/0500-0599/HB0524IN.htm)
provenance.note: No passage vote on record; text read is the bill as filed. Sections 3-5 bring forward other sections only. The Section 1 label has no code number in the text.

operative_text:
Section 1 (uncodified): A public employer of this state or a political subdivision of this state may not adopt or establish a policy prohibiting an employee who has a valid license issued under Section 45-9-101 and a training endorsement as provided by Section 97-37-7 from lawfully carrying a concealed pistol or revolver on any property or in any building under the public employer's control. A sign that is posted by a public employer in accordance with Section 45-9-101 which prohibits the carrying of a concealed pistol or revolver is not effective against any employee of the public employer, provided the employee has a valid license issued under Section 45-9-101 and a training endorsement as provided by Section 97-37-7.
Section 2 (Miss. Code § 45-9-101): However, such sign is not effective against an employee of a public employer who meets the requirements provided in Section 1 of this act.
